svg.title: The same fictional branch-library arrivals under two waiting-line rules
svg.desc: One branch sends 400 jobs and each of three quieter branches sends 20 over an hour. One worker needs 30 seconds per job. Global first-in-first-out finishes 68 of 400 burst-branch jobs and 4 of 20 jobs in each quiet branch within 30 minutes. Branch round robin finishes 34 burst-branch jobs and all 20 in each quiet branch within 30 minutes. Neither meets the promise for all borrowers. This is a local arithmetic model, not SQS or pickup completion.
svg.text: One crowded hour, two waiting-line rules
Fictional arrivals · one non-preemptive worker · 30 seconds per job · 30-minute dispatch-completion target
Same work enters either model
Branch A: 400 jobs/hour
Branches B, C, D: 20 jobs/hour each
Global first-in-first-out
One arrival line; a quiet job can sit behind the burst.
Burst backlog → later quiet arrivals wait
Within 30 minutes of each arrival:
B, C, D: 4 / 20 each
Total: 80 / 460 timely in this toy model
Branch round robin
Rotate among nonempty branch lines; same worker.
Nonempty A, B, C, D lines take turns
Within 30 minutes of each arrival:
B, C, D: 20 / 20 each
Total: 94 / 460 timely in this toy model
Fairer waiting is not more capacity.
Neither rule delivers all jobs in 30 minutes. The model omits pickup stock, retries, storage, AWS behavior and cost.
Original teaching diagram · invented arrival/service assumptions · run queue_window.py to change the case
